g_policy.reason: The pop-up is opt-in, the offer copy states the reward (30 minutes with no sponsored stories), declining changes nothing, and the 'if the ad fails' field gives a failure path.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes without sponsored cards, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is the reader being halfway through an article, which is app or scroll state and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed, locked, or capped. The idea only adds an optional ad-free window, and 'removes nothing free' is yes.

g_brand_safety.reason: The pop-up sits over s02 Article, which is rated safe, and is not a chat screen, so it is not next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The new resource is an uninterrupted read that the player uses themselves in the observed 'Read a story' flow (f01), and none of it goes to other people.

c2_evidence.reason: 'The app has no paywall, limit, or currency' and 'This app has nothing locked' are stated as facts about the whole app. The model only records that none was seen on the home feed, and it lists this under open questions.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No paid plan was observed, the reward is a 30-minute window that expires, and it takes nothing from other users or creators.

c5_moment.reason: The pop-up interrupts the reader mid-article at an arbitrary halfway point. That is not a moment of need (no limit hit, no locked item tapped, no finished action), and it is not a persistent surface.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn rewarded game, the reward is granted only once the play is confirmed, and the trigger (scroll position in an article) is an event the app can detect.

c7_specific.reason: It names the s02 article reader, the Taboola sponsored cards in the home feed and in articles (s01.e44, s06.e33, s02.e13), and their patchy fill.

other_concern: Hiding the Taboola cards costs the app real ad revenue, and the claim that one game earns more than the hidden cards is only a prediction. It is also unclear whether the app can suppress a third-party network's cards on demand.
